title: Tea break & an alert driver: How Kailash pilgrims narrowly escaped Nepal floods
content: Twenty-eight pilgrims from three Indian states safely returned home after escaping Nepal's devastating flash floods. A brief tea break and a ten-minute delay proved crucial in saving their lives. Another group's visa delay inadvertently kept them from the flood zone. They witnessed buses and villages being swept away by the raging waters. Officials are coordinating efforts to rescue other stranded pilgrims from Andhra Pradesh.

title: Influencer who died after being ‘tied to tree, burnt alive’ was 7 weeks pregnant
content: A social media influencer died after suffering severe burn injuries.  She was allegedly abducted and set on fire near Morinda.  Police are searching for two suspects identified in the FIR.  Questions have arisen regarding a potential delay in recording her statement.  An investigation into the circumstances of her death is ongoing.

title: Watch: PM Modi takes part in yoga session during Uzbekistan visit
content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi joined a yoga session in Tashkent on Sunday, where he interacted with attendees and posed for a memorable group photo. Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev extended a warm welcome to the Prime Minister. Delegation-level discussions are planned to focus on trade and defense partnerships, ahead of Modi's participation in the upcoming SCO Summit in Bishkek.

title: ‘Aise bhi log hote hain life me’: Surya reveals Samson’s response after being dropped
content: Suryakumar Yadav spotlighted the encouraging response from Sanju Samson after he was left out of the 2026 World Cup roster. Samson's commitment to prepare as if he were part of the squad gave the team a considerable confidence boost. His later heroic contributions in the knockout rounds were pivotal, culminating in his recognition as Player of the Tournament.

title: 'Frustrated' elderly father, friend kill schizophrenic son in Delhi
content: A father and his friend were arrested for allegedly killing his son in Kalindi Kunj. The 64-year-old father claimed his schizophrenic son had become aggressive and unmanageable. Investigators found the victim's body with head injuries and signs of strangulation. The accused lured the victim to an abandoned container before assaulting him. Police recovered the murder weapon and bloodstained clothing from the scene.

title: Bryan Johnson who wanted to live forever now wants same for dogs
content: Tech entrepreneur Bryan Johnson is extending his anti-aging focus to canine longevity. He plans to make his dog Katara the most measured dog globally. Johnson believes improving dog diets can significantly enhance their health and lifespan. Canine and human biology share many parallels, aiding wellness research. Veterinary drug approvals move faster, accelerating scientific validation for treatments.

title: Tilak Varma in India’s ODI World Cup plans as selectors seek Shreyas Iyer backup
content: As India's team management strategizes for the upcoming ODI World Cup, they're considering Tilak Varma as a valuable middle-order backup. His left-handed batting style could enhance the team's dynamics, alongside his potential bowling skills. With the New Zealand tour approaching in October, selectors aim to ensure optimal batting positions, seeking both stability and depth in the squad.

title: Meta explored 60% layoffs in plan hatched at Zuckerberg's Hawaii compound
content: Meta explored cutting some teams by up to 60% and handing their work to AI agents under a plan code-named Project OT. Hatched at Mark Zuckerberg's Hawaii retreat, it involved two layoff waves, pods of three replacing traditional teams, and keystroke tracking to train AI models. Staff revolted, internal sentiment fell from 74% to 55%, and Meta's own data showed the AI wasn't delivering promised productivity gains.

title: Oklahoma woman's $1,373 power bill tops rent, sparks petition over soaring costs
content: As intense summer heat sweeps through the region, many households are grappling with skyrocketing electricity bills. Raelynn McMurchy's monthly statement doubled, igniting discussions on much-needed policy reforms. Oklahoma's power provider continues to disconnect customers in alarming numbers, leaving local charities to struggle for emergency support. Residents are calling for robust measures to prevent power shutoffs during the scorching months.

title: 'Bill Gates wrong about robot tax': Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang
content: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang disagrees with Bill Gates' robot tax proposal. Huang believes AI will create more jobs overall, not fewer. He suggests companies with increased productivity tend to hire more people. Huang sees a future of reindustrialization with demand for skilled labor. This new economic era will create many jobs across various sectors.

title: AAP leader Gurpreet Singh shot dead in Punjab; 4 assailants flee in car
content: An Aam Aadmi Party leader, Gurpreet Singh, was fatally shot by four armed assailants. The incident occurred in Mamdot, Punjab, on Saturday evening while he was in a car. Singh was declared dead upon arrival at the Civil Hospital after the attack. Another man, Harpreet, sustained injuries and was referred for further treatment. Police are actively investigating the shooting and seeking to identify the perpetrators.

title: Italian jobs, French connections and Berlin walls: Chess’s European tour
content: Sicily, Madrid, France and Berlin have all left their mark on chess vocabulary. The Sicilian Defence dates back to Giulio Cesare Polerio, while Ruy López gave the Spanish Opening one of its first systematic analyses. The French Defence emerged from a 1834 correspondence match between Paris and London. Berlin Defence, meanwhile, was revived by Vladimir Kramnik in his 2000 world championship match against Garry Kasparov.

title: Joe Root scripts history vs Pak at Lord’s, surpasses Ponting’s all-time record
content: Joe Root has made history by scoring the most Test runs for England, eclipsing Ricky Ponting's record in a thrilling match against Pakistan. This landmark not only highlights Root's outstanding performance in his home Tests but also sets him on the path to chase Sachin Tendulkar's overall record as England triumphs in the series at Lord's.

title: Kim Jong UN shakes up North Korea’s military, dismisses defence minister
content: North Korea has shaken up its military hierarchy by removing the defense minister, a move approved by Kim Jong Un in a recent leadership meeting. This change mirrors advancements at the nation's weapons research center, which has introduced new combat weapon systems. As tensions rise, trilateral military drills involving South Korea, the US, and Japan will carry on, designed to counter North Korea's ongoing nuclear and missile provocations.

title: Bank holidays in September: When and where will banks remain closed? Check list
content: In September, banks throughout India will close for various festive occasions. On September 4th, multiple states will celebrate Janmashtami, resulting in branch closures. Following this, Ganesh Chaturthi on September 14th and 15th will also see numerous banks shut across different regions. Additional local holidays and elections will contribute to this schedule. However, customers can continue to access ATMs and digital banking services during these times.

title: US-Venezuela energy pact: What we know about Trump’s ‘biggest oil deal in world history’

Under this agreement, rights to unexplored oil reserves will be held for a century, with the U.S. claiming fifty-five percent of the new venture's output. This collaboration promises to inject significant investments and generate tax income for Venezuela.

This trip underscores India’s dedication to nurturing historical connections and fostering prosperity for all involved nations.

Specialist teams used expedition skills to access disaster zones where roads had disappeared.  Rescuers entered a mud-choked hydropower tunnel, pushing approximately 120 meters inside.  They recovered a camera bag and determined excavation equipment was needed for deeper access.  The rescue operations aimed to locate workers trapped in multiple hydropower tunnel systems.

title: ‘ I take the blame myself’: Suryakumar Yadav’s big regret over failed ODI career

His wife, Steffi Graf, who also faced the rigorous demands of elite sports, shared this perspective, allowing them to focus on nurturing their children's individual passions.

The Chiefs star has interests in Garage Beer, valued at around $200 million, Sleep Number and 1587 Prime, alongside a new NIL venture called TEKTA. He has also joined the ownership group of the Cleveland Guardians, adding MLB to his expanding portfolio. Kelce's moves show a clear focus on investments, ownership and businesses that can outlast his football career.

The move has a personal connection for the Kansas City Chiefs star, who grew up in Ohio near Cedar Point and has long loved theme parks. The investment comes as the company faces financial challenges, while Kelce continues building interests beyond football, including Formula 1 and brand partnerships.

title: Nepal fights time, terrain to save 500 feared trapped in six hydro projects

The Nepalese army and armed police are on the ground conducting rescue missions, yet inclement conditions and accessibility issues pose significant hurdles. They are leveraging technology, including drones and drilling rigs, to locate and assist the stranded individuals effectively.

title: Nepal floods: 4 at hydropower tunnel among 108 Indians rescued; toll 682

title: August rainfall fails to reduce India's monsoon deficit
content: India's cumulative monsoon rainfall deficit remains despite August's better-than-expected rains.  This deficit has caused a significant acreage gap in kharif crop sowing.  Paddy and maize acreage have both reported notable declines compared to last year.  Erratic rainfall distribution prevented increased acreage for most kharif crops.  Several states, including Bihar and Andhra Pradesh, face substantial rainfall deficits.

In light of the publicized ruling, the court mandated the submission of separate affidavits from the involved officers to detail their positions.

Earlier reviews also found violations in other masala products from Everest.  These actions highlight ongoing food safety scrutiny within the Indian market.

title: 4.9-magnitude earthquake hits Afghanistan near Hindu Kush
content:
Earthquake hits Afghanistan near Pak border

A 4.9-magnitude earthquake struck Afghanistan on Sunday morning, according to the National Centre for Seismology (NCS). The earthquake was recorded at 9.36 am IST, with its epicentre located near Hindu Kush range on Afghanistan-Pakistan border. The quake took place at a depth of 147 km beneath the Earth's surface. There were no immediate reports of casualties or damage.
